quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 half-year report (DART, filed 08-14-2026, consolidated): H1 revenue KRW 8,985,938M (vs KRW 8,317,595M in H1 2025, +8.0%), operating profit KRW 547,774M (vs KRW 413,581M, +32.4%), net income KRW 286,594M (vs KRW 176,652M); Q2 alone revenue KRW 4,724,808M (vs KRW 4,569,021M), OP KRW 314,260M (vs KRW 271,106M), NI KRW 226,368M. Segment H1 net revenue: Doosan Enerbility power segment KRW 4,087,322M (45.49%, OP KRW 154,439M vs KRW 91,018M a year earlier), Doosan Bobcat KRW 4,694,956M (52.25%, OP KRW 498,727M), Doosan Fuel Cell KRW 172,667M (OP loss KRW 52,205M). Exports 80.08% of revenue (KRW 7,195,579M). Power-segment contract revenue by region: Korea KRW 1,389,499M, Middle East KRW 1,582,513M, Europe KRW 614,565M, Asia KRW 406,742M, Americas KRW 224,153M. Separate (parent) H1 revenue KRW 3,760,610M, OP KRW 199,640M. One customer group (Group A) accounted for KRW 1,518,623M of consolidated revenue (>10%); on the parent basis Group A KRW 1,491,207M, Customer B KRW 194,417M, Customer C KRW 181,362M. Corporate bond rating raised from BBB+ to A- by Korea Ratings (05-08-2026) and NICE (06-24-2026). Operating cash flow -KRW 886,652M on working-capital build (unbilled contract assets +KRW 817,966M, inventories +KRW 442,684M).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 rev KRW 8,985.9B (+8.0% YoY); OP KRW 547.8B (+32.4%); Q2 rev KRW 4,724.8B; power segment H1 rev KRW 4,087.3B / OP KRW 154.4B

quarterly_data.signal: ORDER BACKLOG KRW 29,680.8B at 06-30-2026 (vs KRW 25,502.5B at 01-01-2026); Doosan Enerbility segment KRW 27,501.8B (headline: Czech Dukovany units 5&6 NSSS), up from KRW 23,393.1B on KRW 8,271.3B of H1 additions less KRW 4,162.6B recognised as revenue. GAS TURBINES: 12 units ordered in H1 2026 (5 domestic, 7 overseas) bringing cumulative Doosan large-GT contracts to 24 units / >10.7GW, incl. a 4.6GW US order; domestic GT share 96.5% (2025: 53.4%), overseas 9.0% (2025: 2.1%); two further large-GT package supply contracts filed 12-17-2025 and 03-06-2026 with customer and amount withheld; filing states large-GT demand exceeds supply and major GT makers are investing to expand capacity, while customers are pre-paying reservation deposits to lock supply. New H1 2026 awards: Oman Duqm IPP 870MW CCPP (Coastal Power SAOC, signed 06-12-2026, KRW 476,368M), Oman Misfah IPP (Jabel Power SAOC, 06-12-2026, KRW 1,005,227M consolidated), Saudi Jafurah Phase II cogeneration with Korea Electric Power Corporation (06-01-2026, KRW 837,040M), Boryeong new CCPP main equipment (Korea Midland Power, KRW 281,600M). Nuclear backlog: Dukovany 5&6 NSSS KRW 5,063,505M (6.43% complete, to 04-18-2038), Dukovany turbine-generator KRW 724,652M, El-Dabaa NPP KRW 2,474,915M (27.63%), Shin-Hanul 3&4 reactor equipment KRW 2,387,981M (37.51%), Shin-Hanul 3&4 main construction KRW 1,019,982M. Offshore wind: 1,203MW of Doosan 8/10MW turbines confirmed incl. Yeosu Geumodo 160MW and Incheon Gureopdo 250MW won in the H1 2026 fixed-price auction; Yeonggwang Yawol offshore wind EPC KRW 575,000M (signed 12-31-2025). Filing cites IEA power demand growth of 3.6%/yr for 2026-2030 driven by AI data centres, and 96GW of gas-combined-cycle orders in 2025 (+41%).
quarterly_data.figure: Backlog KRW 29.68T (+4.18T YTD); power segment KRW 27.50T; 24 GTs / >10.7GW cumulative, 12 GT orders in H1 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity (H1 2026, annual capacity pro-rated 2/4): reactors and steam generators 3,500MW (1,400MW x 5 units), steam turbines 3,000MW domestic + 605MW overseas (Skoda), GAS TURBINES 1,520MW (380MW/unit x 8 units per year, assembly-stand basis), generators 4,500MW, BOP 1,750MW, wind turbine components 110MW (DS205 10MW x 22 units/yr), castings 11,000t and forgings/special steel 72,150t. Utilisation: turbines/nuclear 80.0% (249,242 of 311,482 man-hours), castings/forgings 66.2% (55,015t of 83,150t). Filing says the company is securing timely production capacity as nuclear and gas-turbine businesses scale up, shortening manufacturing lead times and expanding/diversifying the supply chain. CAPEX: H1 2026 power-segment plant expansion KRW 59,183M plus technology development KRW 53,453M; 2026-2028 plan KRW 1,198,198M for plant new-build/expansion (KRW 403,283M in 2026, KRW 568,692M in 2027, KRW 226,223M in 2028) earmarked for SMR, GT and wind facilities, plus KRW 424,199M technology development (GT, wind). Dedicated SMR factory new-build and innovative-manufacturing facility (disclosed 12-17-2025) has completed basic design, detailed design in progress. Raw materials (H1 2026 vs 2025 avg): steel plate KRW 979/kg (vs 900), aluminium KRW 5,124/kg (vs 3,813), scrap KRW 601/kg (vs 493), Fe-Mo KRW 57,775/kg (vs 44,114), nickel KRW 27,727/kg (vs 21,969); filing attributes Q2 moves to rising AI-infrastructure investment, US-Iran war supply-chain disruption (Hormuz closure hitting Middle East aluminium smelters) and Korean anti-dumping tariffs on Chinese steel. Power-segment material and subcontracting purchases KRW 3,223,355M in H1. Consolidated PP&E additions KRW 227,949M; KRW 397,427M of construction-in-progress transferred to operating assets.
quarterly_data.figure: GT capacity 8 units/yr (380MW each); turbine/nuclear utilisation 80.0%; KRW 1,198.2B plant capex 2026-28 for SMR/GT/wind

quarterly_data.signal: R&D: KRW 209,948M in H1 2026 (2.34% of revenue), 280 projects. Key programmes: 300H S2 gas turbine (H+ class model), 100%-hydrogen combustor for large GT (scale-up from mid-size model), mid-size 100%-hydrogen GT demonstration, NuScale SMR automatic-welding process optimisation, ultra-large PM-HIP core technology for SMR, high-speed cladding welding (>200% productivity), Korean 10MW wind supply-chain localisation, aero-engine (turbojet/turbofan/turbogenerator) development, additive manufacturing for aerospace/defence. SMR: after NuScale material orders the company is pursuing NuScale equipment manufacturing orders and is in talks with multiple other SMR designers; holds 0.69% of NuScale Power (KRW 30,181M) and 0.30% of X-Energy (KRW 24,155M). Doosan's own large GT has been in commercial operation at Gimpo cogeneration since 07-2023; Boryeong new CCPP (569MW) due for completion in 2026; GTs designed for hydrogen fuel conversion with utility demonstrations under way. New independent director Min Won-ki (AI expert, former Vice Minister of Science and ICT) appointed 03-31-2026 to drive AI transformation of products and manufacturing; PwC engaged for AI-productivity work (KRW 1,200M, 02-2026 to 04-2026). Board approved participation in Doosan Tesna semiconductor test plant new-build (04-28-2026). Shareholder returns: bought back 1,332,350 shares for KRW 130,343M (04-02-2026 to 04-15-2026) for employee stock compensation; no dividend, board says returns will be reviewed once core growth investments (large nuclear, GT, steam turbine, SMR capacity) are funded.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 R&D KRW 209.9B (2.34% of sales); 300H S2 H+ GT and hydrogen GT programmes; SMR plant in detailed design

Related parties: 15% stake in Tuwaiq Casting & Forging Company (Saudi) with H1 sales of KRW 10,440M and a SAR 239,813K loan guarantee; Doosan Fuel Cell is the parent's fuel-cell supplier (H1 purchases KRW 16,439M) and began SOFC stack exports to Germany in H1 2026 and supplies HyAxiom (US). Group purchases from Doosan Corp (IT systems, trademark) KRW 18,522M. Subsidiaries: Doosan Skoda Power (67%, Czech, steam turbines), Doosan Turbomachinery Services (US, La Porte TX), Doosan ATS America (GT combustor/compressor R&D centre), Doosan GridTech (US grid software, H1 loss KRW 20,336M).
